transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Um… I came in because my mind keeps going blank, and it’s been scaring me. Like at work, I’ll be looking right at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, things I’ve done for years, and suddenly I can’t remember what step comes next.

It’s like the whole sequence just disappears. And then I start thinking about how everyone driving by expects me to know exactly what I’m doing, and—sorry, there was this one time with a pickup truck and cones all over the place—but the main thing is, my thinking just kind of shuts off at the worst times.
Have you ever felt like the world around you seems unreal or detached, or as if you're observing yourself from outside your body?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I’d call it outside my body. Sometimes things feel kind of off when I’m overwhelmed, but maybe that’s just me losing track of what I’m supposed to be doing. Like when the traffic pattern changes and everyone’s waiting, and then I’m thinking about the timing of the signs instead of—sorry, I’m not answering right.

I haven’t really noticed feeling like I’m floating above myself or watching myself, no. The “unreal” part… I’m not sure what you mean exactly.
Can you think of a time when the world around you felt strange or unreal, like you were in a dream or things weren’t quite real?

I’m trying to think… I don’t know if I’ve had it like a dream exactly. Sometimes when I’m standing there with the traffic and the radios going, everything gets sort of… too much, and then I can’t tell if I’m focusing on the cones or the cars or what I’m supposed to say next.

But I wouldn’t say the world feels fake. It’s more like I get scrambled. Like once I was watching the line of cars back up near a school zone, and I started thinking about whether the kids were getting out early that day, and then about this parent who yelled at me last winter—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

No, I don’t think I’ve noticed things feeling unreal like a dream. I just get confused or overwhelmed, I guess.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from the outside, even just for a moment?

I don’t think so… not like watching myself from outside. I mean, sometimes I’m doing something and it feels like I’m not fully keeping up with myself, if that makes sense, like my hands are there and the sign is there and I’m supposed to be paying attention to the lane… and then I start worrying I missed something.

But no, I haven’t really had that feeling of being outside myself looking down or anything. At least I don’t think I have.
Have you ever experienced moments where you felt detached from your own thoughts, body, or feelings, like you were numb or not fully connected to yourself, even if just for a short time?

I’m not sure… numb, maybe, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean. Like sometimes I’ll be standing there and I realize I haven’t really noticed my shoulders are tight, or my feet hurt, because I’m trying to keep track of the cars and the timing and whether someone’s about to turn when they shouldn’t.

But detached from my thoughts or body… I don’t think so. Not like I’m disconnected from myself. It’s more like I get overwhelmed and then everything gets jumbled, and I might feel kind of blank for a second, but I’m still there. I don’t know if that counts.
Has there ever been a time when you felt like you were disconnected from yourself, like your body didn’t feel like your own, or like you were in a fog or dream, even just for a few moments?

I don’t think so… I mean, foggy, maybe in the sense that I get kind of overloaded and then I’m not tracking things right, but not like my body isn’t mine. That sounds… different than what I’ve had, I think.

Sometimes when there’s a lot going on, like people honking or someone waving at me when they’re not supposed to—well, they do that all the time, especially if they’re late, like that’s somehow my fault—but I’ll get sort of blank for a second. Then I’m thinking, wait, did I already switch the sign, did I check that side, and I have to pull myself back.

But disconnected from myself, like a dream or my body not feeling like mine… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even if just for several days in a row?

Yeah… I mean, most mornings I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest. Like before I even get out of bed, it already feels like the whole day is ruined.

It’s weird because the alarm goes off and I’ll just lie there thinking about stupid little things, like whether my uniform is in the dryer or if the neighbor’s dog is barking again, and then suddenly it’s like… no, it’s not really about that. It’s just this weight. It’s there before anything even happens.
Have you lost interest or felt less pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?

Yeah… I have. I used to be the person who would set things up, you know? Like if the choir needed rides, I’d be the one texting people and figuring out who had room in their car. Or the garden swaps, I used to get excited about who was bringing tomato starts or basil, and with youth basketball I’d be the snack person, making sure nobody forgot oranges or water bottles.

Now I’ll just sit there with my phone in my hand for hours, looking at messages, and I don’t answer. Not because I’m mad at anybody. I just… don’t feel that push to do it. Like the part of me that used to care enough to get moving is just not there.
Have you had a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things, and these feelings were present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… yes. It’s not just a bad morning here and there. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness in my chest, like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor.

And then I’ll start thinking about little things, like whether my shoes are by the door or if I left my badge in the car, and it’s like those things aren’t even the real problem. The sadness is already there. It stays with me… most of the day, a lot of days.
